chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Husayn, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the khifaf (leather footwear) that are sold in the market, and he said: “Buy them and perform salat (prayer) in them until you come to know that it is carrion itself specifically.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام, the one being asked for the ruling
key_terms.السُّوقِ: the marketplace where such items are commonly sold
key_terms.الْخِفَافِ: leather footwear or khuffs sold for use
key_terms.اِشْتَرِ: buy it; an instruction indicating permissibility
key_terms.بِعَيْنِهِ: specifically and with certainty in that very item
key_terms.صَلِّ: perform salat (prayer); indicating the item may be worn in prayer
key_terms.مَيِّتٌ: carrion, meaning from an animal dead without lawful slaughter

ai.seo_question: Can one buy leather footwear from the market and perform salat (prayer) in it without knowing its origin?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning leather footwear sold in the market. It indicates permissibility and the validity of salat (prayer) in them unless one knows specifically that the leather came from a dead animal not slaughtered according to the law.
